speaker: Buck
teaser: Forty years of duck hunting. Now the ducks sneak up on him.
hello: Buck Shotwell. Forty years in a duck blind, every frosty dawn I could get.
Lately the ducks sneak up on me. And the wife says my left ear's gone on strike.

which_ear.say: The left, no contest. The phone lives on my right ear these days.
which_ear.note: Worse on the left; phone lives on the right

onset.say: Slow. Crept up over the years, like fog on the marsh. Nothing sudden.

ringing.say: A high whine in both ears. Louder on the left. Like a mosquito that never lands.
ringing.note: Whine in both ears, louder on the left

red_flags.say: No pain, no leaking, no spinning. Steady as a wooden decoy.

say: Forty years of duck hunting. Twelve-gauge on my right shoulder.
Earplugs? Never. Figured I'd miss the ducks talking.
noise.note: 40 years of shotguns, right-handed, no plugs

ear_history.say: Never had an ear infection. No operations, never took a knock to the head.

family.say: My dad got a bit deaf. Mind you, he ran a sawmill for thirty years.
family.note: Dad had some loss; he ran a sawmill

health.say: Fit as a fiddle. One little pill for cholesterol. That's the lot.

aids.say: Never. The wife's been on at me for years. My retriever doesn't nag.

say: The wife, when she sits on my left in the truck.
And at dawn I can't hear the wings whistle any more. The ducks are on me before I see 'em.
hardest.note: Wife on his left side; can't hear duck wings

right.caption: Buck's RIGHT ear: a clean canal and a pearly, healthy eardrum. Not a feather in sight.

left.caption: Buck's LEFT ear: just as clean and healthy. It looks exactly like the right one.

decision_lines.fit: Not yet! A left ear this much worse is a red flag. Doctor first, then fit.
decision_lines.refer: Refer! The shotgun likely did it, but ears this lopsided need a doctor's all-clear first.
decision_lines.today: Nothing sudden: it crept in over forty seasons. A doctor soon, not today.
decision_lines.clear: No aids? His left ear sits near 60 dB up high. He needs help, after the doctor.

why.prompt: Why does Buck see a doctor before hearing aids?
options: His left ear is much worse than his right.
Right! A clear difference between ears is a red flag, even when gunfire likely explains it.
Unmasked bone showed a gap in his left ear.
That 'gap' was his right cochlea answering. Masked bone sat on the air: no gap.
Ringing in both ears is a red flag.
Ringing in both ears is common with noise. Ringing in ONE ear only is the flag.
Hearing loss from shooting always needs a doctor.
Not always. Matching noise loss in both ears can be fitted. Here it's the mismatch that flags.

debrief: Shooter's ear is real: the ear nearer the muzzle takes the blast. For right-handers, that's the left.
But a lopsided loss is a red flag until a doctor clears it. Even with a good excuse.
Earplugs AND earmuffs, every shot from now on. The damage so far stays; more is preventable.
goodbye: Here's a letter for the ear doctor, with your chart. Once you're cleared, come back and we fit.
A doctor for my ears? Fine. Long as nobody tells me to quit hunting.
Keep hunting! Just plug AND muff. Electronic muffs even let you hear the ducks coming.
Muffs that let the ducks through? Sold. See you after the doctor, owl.

headlines.S: BUCK STOPS HERE: LOPSIDED EARS SEE DOCTOR
headlines.A: DUCK HUNTER REFERRED; EARMUFFS IN SEASON
headlines.B: BUCK REFERRED; A FEW STAMPS FLEW THE NEST
headlines.C: CHART WINGED, NOT BAGGED, SAYS OWL
headlines.Do-over: SITTING DUCK: BUCK'S WORKUP NEEDS A RESHOOT

subheads.S: Left far worse than right, masked bone on the left, and a doctor before any fitting.
subheads.A: Shooter's ear is real, but a lopsided loss still sees a doctor first.
subheads.B: The right call, though a few stamps strayed: mask the bone when one ear is much worse.
subheads.C: Unmasked bone hears the better cochlea, so mask it to type the poorer ear.
subheads.Do-over: A lopsided loss means a doctor first, gunfire or not; Buck will be back at dawn.
